pinterest.title: The Gloria Tornado: a backseat memory from a 1990s Texas childhood
pinterest.description: A six-year-old's memory from the back seat of a forest green Pontiac on a winding Texas dirt road, told as memoir. Narrative nonfiction about family and memory from Not Plain, a memoir newsletter by Sarah.

slides.text: It’s a hot summer day. My family is living in a small Texas town, and I’m 6 years old.

slides.label: Gloria
slides.text: I’m dressed and watching Gloria tornado through the house — of course it’s stressful, everything always is, and of course we’re late.

slides.label: the forest green Pontiac
slides.text: Finally, she loads us into the forest green Pontiac.

slides.label: the driver’s seat
slides.text: My mom gets in the driver’s seat and throws her things — she always has so many things — into the passenger seat, and we’re off.

slides.label: blackberry bushes
slides.text: The road is lined with blackberry bushes and overgrown trees, two big berms on either side to help prevent flooding when it rains.
We haven’t gone far when the car screeches to a halt.
